coaching.title: Active Recovery + Strength
coaching.message: Calendar says Week 5 recovery day off yesterday's B2B day 2 — 24 days to Julian Alps. Optional 20-30 min very easy jog or brisk walk, Zone 1 only (cap around 120 bpm, nose-breathing pace). If the legs feel flat from the back-to-back, walk it and lose nothing. Then Strength Session 1: single-leg work (split squats, step-downs), hip stability, core, and eccentric calf/quad loading — that eccentric work is exactly what buys you the 2500m of Julian Alps descent. Cieneguilla sits around 1000m, so the easy stuff will feel slightly harder than sea level; go by feel, not pace. Everything today is protection for the weekend race simulation.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Low-load day, but not a low-carb day — you're still refilling glycogen from the back-to-back block and loading for the weekend simulation. Target ~220g carbs and 1.6-2.0 g/kg protein spread across 4 feedings (30-40g per sitting) to drive repair. Front-load carbs earlier in the day, add anti-inflammatory foods — Peru makes this easy: quinoa, sweet potato/camote, avocado, fresh fish, papaya. Salt normally and drink to thirst plus a bit extra at altitude. No gels needed today; save the gut training for the weekend.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: The descents yesterday left microtrauma in the quads — treat that as the priority. Ten minutes of easy foam rolling on quads, calves, and glutes (pressure, not pain), then legs up the wall for 8-10 minutes. Skip deep static stretching on freshly-loaded tissue. Sleep is the real session today: 8+ hours, room dark and cool, and no screens the last 30 minutes. If soreness is still above a 4/10 tomorrow morning, that's data for how you pace the weekend simulation.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 24 days out — the fitness is already banked. Nothing you do today makes you faster in Kranjska Gora; everything you do today makes you able to execute the weekend simulation, which does. That's the discipline that separates finishers from racers: taking the easy day genuinely easy. Use the quiet to rehearse the race — picture yourself 3 hours into the Julian Alps, power-hiking a steep pitch with a calm heart rate, knowing you practiced exactly this. Restraint today is aggression later.
